questions.question: Where are instance variables normally declared?

options.value: In the class body, outside methods and constructors

questions.explanation: Instance fields belong to each object and are declared at class scope.

questions.question: What does private on a field mean?

options.value: Direct access is restricted to the declaring class
The field cannot change at all
The field is shared by every object

questions.explanation: Private controls visibility, not mutability or whether the field is static.

questions.question: What does a public method offer?

options.value: An operation accessible to permitted client code
A local variable for every class

questions.explanation: Public methods form the class’s accessible interface.

questions.question: Which declaration represents per-object whole-number state?
questions.explanation: The declaration creates an instance field when it lacks static.

questions.question: What is the default initial value of an int instance field?
questions.explanation: Unlike uninitialized local variables, int fields receive a default zero.

questions.question: What is the default initial value of a reference instance field?
questions.explanation: No object is created merely by declaring a reference field.

questions.question: Must every class define a main method to be useful?

options.value: Only classes with private fields need main
Only classes with constructors need main
No, other classes can construct and use its objects
Yes, all classes must run independently

questions.explanation: A supporting class can provide a reusable type without an entry point.

questions.question: What is the purpose of accessor methods?
questions.explanation: An accessor typically returns information without changing the receiver.
get returns the receiver’s initialized instance field.

questions.question: Two Counter objects each start at 2. Only the first is incremented once. What is the second object’s count?
questions.explanation: Instance state is separate for separately constructed objects.
